title: TASK-universal-media-decomposer-A: MAJOR_ISSUES_RAISE — contract-method docstring gaps + stale README scope + CONTRACTS.md drift
body:
Round-1 foundation docs analysis (all 13 steps complete). Not a PASS. Findings:

1. Missing docstrings on 5 of 10 binding CONTRACTS.md methods: SegmentRegistry.register (src/umd/segmentation/registry.py:173), LocatorResolver.resolve (src/umd/resolution/locator_resolver.py:146), AuditService.explain (src/umd/audit/service.py:94), StageRunRepository.claim (src/umd/storage/postgres/stage_repository.py:95), JobRunAudit.record (src/umd/storage/postgres/stage_repository.py:200). CurrentStateReducer.reduce class method (src/umd/storage/postgres/reducer.py:398) also lacks its own docstring (module fn reduce_current_state is documented). Class/module docstrings state the binding contract, so semantics are recoverable, but the public methods themselves are bare.

2. README.md scope drift: says "implements Phase 1" and "Phase 2/3 (domain models, locators, event schemas, reducers, handlers, ingestion API) are intentionally out of scope here" (README.md:4,56-57) — but Phases 2-3 are fully implemented (domain/models.py, domain/locators.py, schemas/events/ 20 files, storage/postgres/reducer.py, application/commands.py, application/ingestion.py; 110 tests pass). Layout section also omits schemas/, segmentation, resolution, audit, jobs, application packages.

3. CONTRACTS.md:8 documents SourceStore.get_range(source_ref, locator) but implementation is get_range(source_ref, start=0, length=None, *, version=None) (src/umd/storage/ocfl/store.py:168). Binding-contract signature drift; plan P1-S3 note already re-expresses it as (source_ref, start, length) — contract file needs reconciliation (design decision, not DocsGenerator).

4. Minor: tables.py module docstring documents ownership constraints but does not enumerate the 22 tables (present via section banners + inline comments only); reducer.py:4 docstring has a double-backtick formatting glitch `(:meth:`CurrentStateReducer.replay``).

Verified ACCURATE (no drift): put_immutable content-addressing/no-filename-key, get_range bound-capping + full-object fixity, reducer totality (None row -> concrete row), claim idempotency (already_exists, won=False), JobRunAudit excluded from semantic replay (reducer NON_SEMANTIC + events NON_SEMANTIC_EVENT_TYPES + stage_repository module docstring). Config/env (config.py class docstrings + .env.example all 11 UMD_ vars), Makefile help+comments, migration 0001 docstring/revision metadata, conftest UMD_TEST_POSTGRES gating all present and accurate. Event schemas well-formed (draft-2020-12, additionalProperties:false, required; v1->v2 upcaster consistent).

Routing: MAJOR_ISSUES_RAISE — fixes span three artifact classes with different ownership (source docstrings, README editorial scope, binding-contract file); README fundamentally misrepresents delivered scope; CONTRACTS.md requires a design-owner decision. No generation cycle dispatched.

(b) README.md now accurately describes Phases 1-3 foundation scope, layer authority line, Makefile commands, 110 full-suite tests (verified: pytest --collect-only = 110), 22 tables (verified count in tables.py), JSONB vector placeholder, append-only triggers on semantic_event AND embedding (verified in migrations/versions/0001_initial_core.py), StageRun claim authority, no-projection-writes ingestion; does not claim Phases B-F implemented. title: store.py get_range '*LOCK*' comment is copy-paste noise
body: src/umd/storage/ocfl/store.py get_range lines 193-196 contain: 'The ``*LOCK*`` free invariant is that a single read respects ONE hard buffer cap...' — '*LOCK*' is the reducer LOCK_PREDICATE concept, completely unrelated to OCFL bounded reads. Appears to be copy-paste noise from the reducer module. Confusing code comment (not a docstring; behavior IS correctly bounded by _read_bounded + max_read_buffer_bytes cap). Flag for fixer to clarify/remove; not a docs-dispatch item.

title: CONTRACTS vs code: CurrentStateReducer naming placement + create_source
body: Two minor contract-vs-code naming observations (semantics all honored — packaging differences permitted by CONTRACTS:3, flagged only as observations, not real drift): (1) CONTRACTS.md:31 'CurrentStateReducer.reduce(current_row, event) -> current_row' — the class method reduce() actually takes (state: CurrentReducedState, event); the pure per-row contract function is module-level reduce_current_state(current_row, event). reducer.py's own docstring correctly frames reduce_current_state as the contract function, so only the CONTRACTS method-name placement differs from code's framing. (2) CONTRACTS.md:9 'SourceRepository.create_source' — surface provides PostgresSourceRepository.get + SourceMembershipService (ensure_source/ensure_work/add_membership) and does honor source/work/continuity/edition/translation/adaptation membership (source table has work_id/continuity_id/edition_id FKs; edition.kind original|translation|adaptation|release; source_membership table). Not real drift. EvidenceRepository.record (CONTRACTS:12) legitimately deferred (extraction is a later cross-plan phase; plan TASK-A does not claim it).

(2) src/umd/storage/postgres/reducer.py line 4: ":meth:`CurrentStateReducer.replay``" has an extra closing backtick (RST role needs exactly one backtick pair; there are four backticks). title: EvidenceRepository.record idempotency doc overstates cross-call dedup
body: PostgresEvidenceRepository.record docstring (src/umd/storage/postgres/repositories.py:196-204) claims: "A row is considered a duplicate (existing) when another row already exists for the same (source_id, locator, evidence_kind, config_digest) — identical extraction output is never inserted twice." The implementation dedups ONLY within a single batch via a local `seen` set (lines 212-226); it never queries the DB for pre-existing rows and the `evidence` table has NO unique index on that tuple (tables.py:267-307). The `if row.inserted_primary_key: created else: existing` branch is dead (inserts always succeed). Cross-call identical extraction output IS inserted twice. Same overstatement in RecordedEvidenceBatch docstring (domain/evidence.py:51-62, "idempotent duplicates of an identical evidence row") and pipeline.py `_config_digest` docstring ("identical runs deduplicate", raster/pipeline.py:99-101). Plan P3-S4 annotation explicitly logged this as a pre-existing Phase 2 gap, but the docstrings overstate rather than disclose it. Answer to verification Q(C) = YES. Requires correction: state in-batch-only dedup + no DB unique index (known limitation).

(2) drain.py:54 references `:func:`umd.jobs.manifest.dag_universe`` — the function is `build_dag_universe` (manifest.py:40). title: sandbox allowed_modules doc overstates enforcement (security-relevant)
body: SandboxPolicy.allowed_modules docstring (src/umd/security/sandbox.py:72-73: "Parser entrypoint modules allowed as -m <module> arguments") implies an enforced allowlist, and dispatch.py:120 sets allowed_modules=(_ENTRYPOINT_MODULE,) believing it restricts the -m entrypoint. But _check_policy (sandbox.py:263-296) NEVER validates argv module membership: allowed_modules appears only at line 279 as a non-emptiness trigger to enable the input-path containment check. Any -m some_other_module passes. Doc/implementation contradiction on a security surface. Resolution ambiguous code-vs-doc: reviewer should decide whether to enforce membership in _check_policy (security-correct) or downgrade the docstring (NOT auto-dispatched to avoid baking in a security downgrade).

title: Env-var doc/deploy drift: compose.yaml + .env.example use single-underscore UMD_POSTGRES_DSN/UMD_OCFL_ROOT which pydantic-settings ignores
body: src/umd/config.py:137-142 uses env_prefix="UMD_" + env_nested_delimiter="__", so nested settings require UMD_POSTGRES__DSN / UMD_OCFL__ROOT / UMD_PROJECTION__VECTOR_HNSW_MIN_VERSION. deploy/compose.yaml:23 (UMD_POSTGRES_DSN), :24 (UMD_OCFL_ROOT), :29 (UMD_VECTOR_HNSW_MIN_VERSION) and .env.example:16,18-19,24,26 use single underscore → silently ignored by the API process. docker-entrypoint.sh:22 reads UMD_POSTGRES_DSN directly so migrations DO target db, but the API falls back to the default 127.0.0.1:5432 and cannot reach the Postgres service → documented compose stack is broken. Same root cause as the 1 failing test (test_app_factory_builds_wired_app_over_real_postgres). docs/deployment.md:44-45 states the nested-with-__ rule correctly but points to the broken examples.

title: README test-count claims stale: 380 passing vs actual 406 passed/4 skipped/1 failed (411 collected)
body: README.md:9-10 "proven by 380 passing tests (plus 2 conditionally skipped...)" and README.md:34 "(380 in the full suite)" are stale. Verified final suite: 406 passed, 4 skipped (docker, kubectl, tesseract×2), 1 FAILED. The README claims a clean pass and undercounts skips. Plan annotations P2-S4 ("379 passed ... 2 skipped") and P3-S4 ("380 full suite") are also stale snapshots vs 411 collected and never mention the failure.

title: README "22-table typed relational core" drift: tables.py defines 23 tables
body: README.md:124 claims "a 22-table typed relational core" but src/umd/storage/postgres/tables.py:5,9-12 declares "23 typed tables" and 23 sa.Table() definitions exist (work, continuity, edition, source, source_membership, segment, evidence, artifact, entity, entity_mention, predicate, semantic_assertion, semantic_event, current_state, current_entity_map, alignment, stage_run, job, job_run_audit, embedding, projection_checkpoint, quarantine, locator_rebase). Off-by-one drift in the user-facing README (plan A annotation recorded 22 when the table was added; count has since grown).

title: Plan G: production.py module docstring overclaims degradation warnings
body: production.py module docstring line 26 claims "a warning is recorded on every degradation". Code contradicts this in at least 3 paths: _basic_segmentation non-text media path (deterministic segments:{id}:root, no warning — arguably intentional), _basic_segmentation text path with no source_store and no committed segments (root ref, no warning), _low_level_extraction baseline fallback evidence_records:{id}:baseline (no warning), _structural_analysis media/reconciled fallback (no warning). Only _format_analysis appends degradation warnings. Doc overclaims observability behavior — MINOR drift, not misleading about correctness.

title: Plan G: docs/api.md missing multipart upload form (new core capability)
body: docs/api.md ingest section (lines 35-40) documents only the inline SourceIngestRequest JSON form. Plan G added the bounded multipart streamed upload (file + media_kind/original_name/work_id/source_id/content_type descriptors, RFC 7807 413 upload_too_large, immutable put_immutable before dispatch) as a headline capability for binary media. A user reading docs/api.md cannot learn binary upload exists. Also analysis response now includes 'stages' not in docs. Candidate for DocsGenerator focused update.

title: Plan G: evidence_refs contract delta documented in migration+handoff, not DD/CONTRACTS
body: DD "Durable stage execution" (line 285) commits "winning stage_run insertion, artifact references, and StageCompleted append in one transaction" — now also evidence_refs. CONTRACTS.md:60 registry contract and DD are not updated, but the delta is thoroughly documented in migrations/versions/0007_stage_run_evidence_refs.py module docstring and handoff-G-to-I-J.md §3/§5. Adequate downstream documentation; CONTRACTS/DD update optional, not blocking.

title: asr-runtime.md under-specifies faster_whisper_runtime_ready() validation (one-word precision fix)
body: deploy/pins/asr-runtime.md:35-36 says the model cache dir is validated by faster_whisper_runtime_ready() as "importable runtime AND cache dir present". The actual function (src/umd/audio/asr.py:299-316) ALSO requires the file model.bin to exist inside the cache dir ("it must contain model.bin (the file the provider actually loads)"). Doc omits the model.bin requirement — reader could conclude an empty cache dir validates. One-word precision fix: "...cache dir present and model.bin present". Minor only: model pin table above already pins model.bin sha256, gate_reason falls through to "model cache not validated", so not user-misleading. All 8 transitive pins in the manifest verified identical to installed versions (faster-whisper 1.2.1, ctranslate2 4.8.1, onnxruntime 1.29.0, tokenizers 0.23.1, huggingface_hub 1.29.0, numpy 2.5.2, av 18.1.0, protobuf 7.36.0); model.bin sha256 matches pin. Plan H round-2 re-review: logged but not dispatched (single minor precision gap; no dispatch-worthy drift).
